overview: Sherwin-Williams, founded in 1866 and headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, develops, manufactures, distributes and sells paint, coatings and related products to professional, industrial, commercial and retail customers, primarily in North and South America with additional operations in the Caribbean, Europe, Asia and Australia. The business is organized into three reportable segments -- Paint Stores Group, Consumer Brands Group and Performance Coatings Group -- anchored by a company-operated store network (4,853 Paint Stores locations plus 307 Consumer Brands stores in Latin America and 317 Performance Coatings branches) that is the industry's largest dedicated professional-paint distribution footprint. FY2025 net sales were $23.57 billion, roughly 80% domestic, across professional contractors, DIY retail, and industrial/OEM customers.

business_model.summary: Sherwin-Williams is a vertically integrated manufacturer-retailer: the Consumer Brands Group makes paint and coatings that are sold mostly through the company's own Paint Stores Group (about 63% of Consumer Brands sales are intersegment transfers), supplemented by third-party retail (home centers, hardware chains) and industrial/OEM channels served by Performance Coatings. Revenue is transactional (project- and purchase-driven, not subscription), but repaint/maintenance demand and a large professional contractor base give it a repeat-purchase, relationship-driven character with high same-store growth consistency.

revenue_streams.name: Paint Stores Group (architectural paint, coatings, contractor/DIY retail)
Performance Coatings Group (industrial, auto refinish, protective & marine, coil, packaging, resins)
Consumer Brands Group (branded/private-label paint sold via third-party retail + LatAm stores)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2B/professional (painting contractors, industrial OEMs, auto body shops, protective/marine applicators) with meaningful B2C/DIY retail through Paint Stores and third-party home centers
business_model.geographic_mix: United States ~80% of net sales; foreign subsidiaries (Canada, Latin America [Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Argentina], Europe, Asia, Australia) ~19.6% of 2025 net sales, growing with the Suvinil (Brazil) acquisition

main_competitors: The Pittsburgh Paints Company (formerly PPG's US/Canada architectural business, sold to American Industrial Partners in Dec 2024)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest paint and coatings company by North American architectural market share and by far the largest dedicated professional paint store network; leading player in Paint Stores Group with an estimated ~25-30%+ share of North American paints and coatings versus PPG's distant second, and this gap widened further after PPG exited US/Canada architectural retail in December 2024

moat_factors.description: 4,853 company-operated Paint Stores give contractors one-stop convenience, credit, color-matching and delivery that competitors' dealer/wholesale models struggle to replicate; Sherwin has opened net new stores every year (80 in 2025, targeting 80-100 in 2026) while PPG shrank its US footprint
Consumer Brands Group manufactures the majority of product sold through Paint Stores (63% intersegment), supporting margin capture and supply control

Sherwin-Williams, Valspar, Krylon, Minwax, Purdy, Dutch Boy and other controlled brands plus long-standing professional painter relationships create switching costs around color programs, credit terms and job-site service

moat_factors.factor: Scale in raw material purchasing and R&D
moat_factors.description: Global sourcing scale and in-house resin/specialty chemical production help offset commodity input volatility relative to smaller regional players

weaknesses: Heavily exposed to cyclical, rate-sensitive end markets (new residential construction, existing home turnover, remodeling)
DIY/Consumer Brands segment has been structurally soft in North America amid weak housing turnover
High and rising financial leverage (net debt ~2.4x EBITDA, above the top of the Company's own 2.0-2.5x target band) funding store growth, buybacks and M&A
Significant unaccrued, open-ended lead pigment/lead-based paint litigation liability with no reasonable estimate of exposure
Latin America/emerging-market currency exposure (e.g., $41.8 million Argentine peso devaluation loss in 2023)

growth_drivers: Continued Paint Stores Group unit growth (targeting ~2% annual store count growth, 80-100 net new US/Canada stores in 2026)

Market share gains from smaller/weaker competitors in a soft demand environment, aided by PPG's December 2024 exit from US/Canada architectural retail and the shutdown of regional players like Kelly-Moore
Latin America expansion via the October 2025 Suvinil (BASF Brazil architectural paints, ~$525M sales) acquisition, adding scale in Brazil, Chile, Mexico and Ecuador
Performance Coatings growth in Protective & Marine, General Industrial, Packaging and Coil as new account wins and favorable mix offset flat core demand
Pricing discipline and simplification/digitization cost initiatives (targeting ~$75 million of 2027 cost savings) to protect margins against raw-material inflation
Eventual housing-market recovery (lower mortgage rates, higher existing-home turnover) as a multi-year demand tailwind not yet reflected in current 'softer-for-longer' results
Continued capital return via buybacks (~$2.4 billion returned to shareholders in 2025) and dividend growth

business.description: Management expects muted demand into 2027 due to elevated mortgage rates, weak existing-home turnover and soft DIY/industrial spending

No single customer exceeds 10% of sales, but losing large accounts in Consumer Brands or Performance Coatings could hurt segment profitability; broad competition from PPG, AkzoNobel, RPM and regional players on price, innovation and service
Suvinil and prior deals (Valspar) must be integrated without diluting margins; Suvinil has already diluted Consumer Brands Group margin (18.3% adjusted vs 23.3% prior year)

financial.description: Total debt of $10.87 billion at year-end 2025, net debt/EBITDA of 2.4x versus a 2.0-2.5x target, with ~$85 million of incremental 2026 interest expense from refinancing and the new HQ/R&D center

Primary exposure to the euro, Brazilian real, Canadian dollar, Mexican peso, British pound, Chinese yuan, Chilean peso and Argentine peso; highly inflationary economies (e.g., Argentina) have caused material one-off losses
Reliance on commercial paper and revolving credit for seasonal working capital; a ratings downgrade would raise borrowing costs

regulatory.description: Decades-old, unaccrued litigation (personal injury, public nuisance, municipal suits) with no reasonable estimate of potential loss; adverse rulings could be material

Active investigation/remediation at current and former sites; a May 2025 Texas AG petition alleges air/water violations tied to a 2023 Garland, TX facility fire, seeking civil penalties and injunctive relief
EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, California climate disclosure laws, and evolving chemical-use regulation could raise compliance costs or require reformulation
Tariffs and import/export restrictions on raw materials and finished goods could raise costs or disrupt supply, particularly given global petrochemical-derived raw material sourcing

macro.description: Mortgage rates remaining elevated even after 2025 Fed cuts continue to suppress new construction and existing-home turnover, the primary architectural paint demand drivers
Resins, latex, solvents and titanium dioxide are largely petrochemical-derived (notably propylene); management expects low-to-mid single digit raw material inflation in 2026-2027
Construction, housing and industrial end markets are cyclical; labor shortages and tariff-driven cost pressure compound demand softness

macro_factors.industry_outlook: US paint and coatings demand has shifted from new-build/DIY toward professional repaint, maintenance and infrastructure spending; the overall market is projected to grow from roughly $34 billion (2024) to $44 billion by 2030, but near-term 2026-2027 growth is muted by high mortgage rates and low housing turnover
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high -- tied to residential construction, existing home sales/turnover, remodeling and industrial production; business is also seasonal (Q2/Q3 generate the majority of sales and earnings)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (indirect) -- mortgage rates and housing turnover are the single largest demand driver for Paint Stores and Consumer Brands; also affects the Company's own borrowing costs given ~$10.9 billion of debt

recent_developments.event: Completed $1.15 billion acquisition of Suvinil, BASF's Brazilian architectural paints business (~$525M annual sales), expanding Consumer Brands Group's Latin America footprint
New global headquarters and R&D center in Cleveland substantially completed and placed into service, adding ~$1.5 billion to PP&E and increasing depreciation/interest expense

Competitor PPG Industries completed the $550 million sale of its US/Canada architectural coatings business (Glidden, Olympic, Pittsburgh Paints) to American Industrial Partners, ceding ground in the segment Sherwin-Williams leads

Texas Attorney General filed suit (amended January 2026) against subsidiary Sherwin-Williams Manufacturing Company alleging environmental violations tied to an August 2023 fire at its Garland, TX facility, seeking civil penalties
Benjamin E. Meisenzahl became Senior Vice President - Finance and CFO

Q3 2026 results: net sales up 7.9% to $6.86 billion (Suvinil-driven Consumer Brands growth +21.7%), adjusted diluted EPS of $3.63 (+1.1%), roughly in line with/slightly below some consensus estimates as gross margin compressed ~140bps on raw material and supply chain cost pressure; FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance narrowed to $11.85-$12.15
Citigroup downgraded SHW to Neutral, reflecting caution on near-term demand
Shares traded in the $300s-$340s range; consensus analyst price targets clustered around $376-$391 with a majority Buy-leaning rating mix

items.target: Up mid-to-high single digit percentage vs. 2025
items.notes: Q4 2026 net sales guided up a mid-single digit percentage vs. Q4 2025
Includes ~$0.82/share Valspar-related acquisition amortization and ~$0.11/share severance/restructuring expense; compares to $10.26 actual in FY2025

items.notes: Midpoint ~$12.00 vs. $11.43 adjusted actual in FY2025

items.target: ~2% of net sales; total 2026 capex expected lower than 2025's $797.6 million
items.notes: New global HQ/R&D center largely complete, reducing capex needs
Driven by refinanced long-term debt, Suvinil-related delayed draw term loans, and new HQ/R&D center financing costs

items.target: 80-100 net new Paint Stores in the US and Canada
items.notes: Consistent with long-term ~2% annual store count growth objective
Planning assumption disclosed alongside Q3 2026 results, alongside expectations of continued soft demand into 2027 and low-to-mid single digit raw material inflation

guidance.management_commentary: Management describes a 'softer-for-longer' demand environment persisting into 2027, with customer sentiment and leading indicators pointing to continued muted demand, particularly in DIY and the Consumer Brands Group. The Company is responding with disciplined pricing actions, cost reduction/simplification initiatives, and continued investment in store growth, digitization and supply chain responsiveness, while maintaining its capital allocation priorities of capex, M&A, dividends and buybacks.

bull_case: Largest, still-expanding professional paint store network widens its moat further as PPG retreats from US/Canada architectural retail and smaller regional players exit the market
Track record of share gains and pricing power even in a soft volume environment, evidenced by FY2025 Paint Stores gross margin and profit growth despite flat-to-down volumes
Suvinil and other bolt-on M&A extend growth into less penetrated, faster-growing Latin American markets
Eventual normalization of mortgage rates and existing-home turnover represents a multi-year demand recovery catalyst not yet priced into a 'softer-for-longer' narrative
Disciplined, consistent capital return (dividends plus ~$2.4 billion of 2025 buybacks) supports per-share earnings growth even when top-line growth is muted
bear_case: Demand softness (high mortgage rates, weak housing turnover, soft DIY) is now guided to persist into 2027, extending a multi-year earnings growth pause
Leverage is above the Company's own 2.0-2.5x net debt/EBITDA target (2.4x at FY2025), funding buybacks, M&A and a large new headquarters even as interest expense rises ~$85 million in 2026
Suvinil acquisition has structurally diluted Consumer Brands Group margins (adjusted segment margin down from 23.3% to 18.3% in Q3 2026), raising integration execution risk
Unaccrued, open-ended lead pigment/lead-based paint litigation represents a tail risk with no visibility into potential liability
Raw material inflation (petrochemical feedstocks, tariffs) and rising SG&A from store growth and restructuring could continue to pressure margins faster than cost-saving initiatives can offset
